questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Which of these Harappan sites is located in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan; Lothal and Dholavira are in Gujarat.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Most Harappan seals were made of which material?
questions.explanation: Steatite, a soft stone, was commonly used for seals.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Terracotta toy models of carts have been found at Harappan sites. What do they suggest?
options: Wheeled carts were used for transport
questions.explanation: The models suggest that wheeled carts were in use.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Harappan weights were generally
options: standardised and made of stone in regular ratios
irregular and different in every village
questions.explanation: Cubical stone weights followed a regular system.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Why do archaeologists consider Harappan cities to have been planned and not randomly grown?
options: Streets, drains and brick sizes follow a consistent pattern
questions.explanation: Consistent layouts and standard brick sizes point to planning.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Shell bangles and beads are found at Harappan sites far from the sea. What is the likely explanation?
options: The raw material was brought by trade or exchange
questions.explanation: Long-distance movement of materials indicates exchange networks.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Name two crafts practised by the Harappans.
questions.answer: Harappan craftspeople made beads, pottery and metal objects. They also made seals and ornaments of shell and stone.
questions.explanation: Excavations show a variety of crafts.

questions.topic: Harappan civilisation
questions.q: Why was Lothal an important Harappan site?
questions.answer: Lothal had a large brick basin regarded as a dockyard, and it was a centre of bead making. Its location made it useful for trade by sea and with other regions.
questions.explanation: Lothal is closely linked with Harappan trade.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: What was the capital of the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra was the imperial capital.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: The mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata belonged to which period?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata lived in the Gupta period.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: Which of these works was written by Kalidasa?
questions.explanation: Abhijnanashakuntalam is a famous play by Kalidasa.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: What were the Mahajanapadas?
options: Sixteen large states of about the sixth century BCE
questions.explanation: Early texts mention sixteen large states, among them Magadha.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: Why was Ashoka's reaction to the Kalinga war significant for state policy?
options: He gave up expansion by war and emphasised Dhamma in dealing with his subjects
questions.explanation: His edicts show a change from conquest to Dhamma.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: Why did Chinese pilgrims like Hsuan Tsang travel to India?
options: To visit Buddhist sites and collect texts
questions.explanation: They came to see Buddhist sacred places and study texts.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: What is a prashasti? Give one example.
questions.answer: A prashasti is a praise poem or inscription glorifying a ruler. The Allahabad pillar inscription praising Samudragupta is an example.
questions.explanation: Prashastis show how rulers wished to be seen and must be read critically.

questions.topic: Early states, Mauryan and Gupta periods, and ancient society
questions.q: Why should historians study inscriptions together with literary texts?
questions.answer: Inscriptions are often contemporary records, while literary texts may have been composed or changed later. Each can reflect the views of its author, so comparing them helps check accuracy and reduce bias.
keyPoints: Texts may be later and biased
questions.explanation: Combining sources gives a more balanced picture.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: Who was the father of the Mughal emperor Akbar?
questions.explanation: Akbar was the son of Humayun.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: In which present-day state is Hampi located?
questions.explanation: Hampi lies in Karnataka.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: What was the role of a Chishti khanqah?
options: A hospice where devotees gathered, shared community meals and heard devotional music
questions.explanation: The khanqah was a centre of spiritual life and charity.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: In the Mughal system, a mansabdar was
options: an imperial officer holding a rank, or mansab
questions.explanation: Mansabdars held ranks that fixed their status, pay and duties.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: Why did Mughal rulers maintain roads and sarais?
options: To aid the movement of armies, officials and merchants, and support trade
questions.explanation: Roads and rest-houses helped administration and commerce.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: Why were coastal ports important to the Vijayanagara Empire?
options: They brought in horses and other goods from abroad and carried out spices and textiles
They were used only by the Mughals
questions.explanation: Overseas trade supplied horses and brought revenue.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: What is langar in the Sikh tradition?
questions.answer: Langar is a community kitchen where free meals are served to all, seated together irrespective of caste or status. It began with the early Sikh Gurus and expresses equality.
keyPoints: People of all backgrounds eat together
questions.explanation: Langar reflects the Sikh emphasis on equality and service.

questions.topic: Medieval India: Mughals, Vijayanagara, Bhakti and Sufi
questions.q: Describe two ways in which Mughal architecture combined different traditions.
questions.answer: Mughal buildings combined Persian elements such as domes, arches and gardens with Indian features such as chhatris and jharokhas. They also used local materials like red sandstone.
questions.explanation: The style blended Persian and Indian traditions.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Which Governor-General introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced it in 1793.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Which Act of 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown?
questions.explanation: The Act of 1858 ended Company rule.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: What could happen to a zamindar's estate under the Permanent Settlement if he failed to pay revenue on time?
questions.explanation: Failure to pay on time could lead to the sale of the estate.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Under the tinkathia system in Champaran, peasants were made to
options: grow indigo on a part of their land for planters
questions.explanation: Planters compelled cultivators to grow indigo on a fixed part of their holdings.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Why did the Company fix revenue permanently in Bengal?
options: To give land to peasants free
To secure a stable income and create a class of landlords loyal to the Company
questions.explanation: A fixed demand gave predictable income and a supportive class.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Why did early nationalist leaders criticise British economic policy?
options: They said it helped Indian industry grow
They argued it drained wealth and harmed Indian industries and peasants
They said India had no economy
questions.explanation: Leaders such as Naoroji argued that colonial policy impoverished India.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: What was the Subsidiary Alliance?
questions.answer: It was a system under which an Indian ruler accepted a British force in his territory and paid for it. He also agreed not to ally with other European powers and kept a British Resident at his court.
keyPoints: Ruler accepts and pays for British troops
questions.explanation: It brought Indian states under British control without direct conquest.

questions.topic: Colonial rule, 1857 and the countryside
questions.q: Why did peasants and artisans join the revolt in some regions in 1857?
questions.answer: Many had lost livelihoods through high revenue demands and cheap imports, and displaced rulers and their dependents also had grievances. Religious fears and anger against the Company added to the discontent.
keyPoints: Heavy revenue and loss of livelihood
questions.explanation: Different groups had their own reasons to join.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: Who gave the slogan Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it?
questions.explanation: The slogan is associated with Tilak.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: In which year did Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
questions.explanation: He returned in 1915.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: The Ahmedabad satyagraha of 1918 was connected with a dispute between
questions.explanation: Gandhi supported the textile workers in their demand.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: Where was the Muslim League founded in 1906?
questions.explanation: The All-India Muslim League was formed at Dhaka in 1906.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: How did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre affect Indian politics?
options: It increased anger against British rule and pushed many towards non-cooperation
questions.explanation: The massacre deepened resentment and fed the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: Why did the Non-Cooperation Movement reach more social groups than earlier movements?
options: It linked local grievances of peasants, workers and students with national demands
questions.explanation: Combining local and national issues widened participation.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: What decision did the Congress take at its Lahore session in 1929?
questions.answer: It declared Purna Swaraj, or complete independence, as its goal. It also decided that 26 January 1930 would be observed as Independence Day.
questions.explanation: The Lahore session set the goal of complete independence.

questions.topic: Gandhi and the national movement
questions.q: Why was the Salt March important for the national movement?
questions.answer: Breaking the salt law was a symbolic and peaceful defiance that anyone could join. It drew mass participation including women, and attracted attention abroad, putting pressure on the government.
questions.explanation: The march turned a simple act into a national protest.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister on 15 August 1947.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: The Preamble describes India as a
questions.explanation: These words describe the character of the Indian state in the Preamble.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Why is India called a republic?
options: Its head of state is a hereditary king
Its head of state is elected and not hereditary
It has no head of state
questions.explanation: A republic has an elected head of state.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Which state was formed in 1953 as the first on a linguistic basis?
questions.explanation: Andhra State was carved out of Madras State in 1953.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Why did the framers adopt universal adult franchise from the start?
options: To restrict voting to the wealthy
To ensure political equality regardless of wealth, education, sex or caste
questions.explanation: Every adult citizen was given an equal vote.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Why is the Indian Constitution a lengthy document?
options: It covers a large and diverse country with detailed provisions on federalism, rights and administration
It was copied word for word from one text
questions.explanation: Detailed provisions were needed for a large federal system.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: State two features of the Indian Constitution.
questions.answer: India has a parliamentary form of government and a federal structure with a strong Centre. The Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights and has an independent judiciary.
questions.explanation: These are widely cited features.

questions.topic: Partition, Independence and the Constitution
questions.q: Why were the first general elections of 1951-52 a major test for democracy in India?
questions.answer: They were held on the basis of universal adult franchise in a vast country where most voters could not read. Organising them involved huge administrative effort, and their peaceful conduct strengthened democratic practice.
questions.explanation: The elections showed that democracy could work at scale.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Who is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Where is the Supreme Court of India located?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court sits in New Delhi.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Which writ directs that a person who has been detained be produced before the court?
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus protects against unlawful detention.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Which writ commands a public authority to perform its duty?
questions.explanation: Mandamus means we command.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: What is the Rajya Sabha's role in respect of a Money Bill?
options: It can reduce it to nothing
It can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha's role on Money Bills is limited to recommendations.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Why is a federal system suitable for a large and diverse country?
options: It allows regional self-rule alongside national unity
questions.explanation: Power is shared so that regions can govern themselves while remaining united.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: What does secularism mean in the Indian context?
questions.answer: The state has no official religion and treats all religions with equal respect. Citizens have freedom to profess, practise and propagate their faith, and the state does not discriminate on the ground of religion.
questions.explanation: Indian secularism means equal treatment of all faiths by the state.

questions.topic: Indian political system: rights, Parliament, judiciary, federalism
questions.q: Why is the Right to Information important for democracy?
questions.answer: It lets citizens obtain information from public authorities, making government more open and accountable. The Right to Information Act of 2005 gave this a legal framework.
questions.explanation: Access to information helps citizens hold government to account.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: In which year was NATO formed?
questions.explanation: NATO was formed in 1949.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in 1961 in
questions.explanation: The first summit took place at Belgrade.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: Glasnost and perestroika were policies introduced in the Soviet Union by
questions.explanation: Gorbachev introduced openness and restructuring in the late 1980s.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: What is the Security Council's primary responsibility?
questions.explanation: The Charter gives it primary responsibility for peace and security.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: Why did many newly independent countries find the Non-Aligned Movement useful?
options: It forced them to join a bloc
It gave them a collective voice and room for independent policies
questions.explanation: Non-alignment strengthened their bargaining position.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: How did the failure of the League of Nations influence the founding of the UN?
options: The League succeeded, so no change was needed
The UN was formed to stop all trade
The League could not prevent the Second World War, so a new body with stronger arrangements was designed
questions.explanation: Lessons from the League shaped the design of the UN.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: What is the full form of ASEAN and what kind of organisation is it?
questions.answer: ASEAN stands for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. It is a regional organisation that promotes economic and political cooperation among its members.
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded in 1967.

questions.topic: World politics: Cold War, UN and regional organisations
questions.q: State two reasons that contributed to the end of the Cold War.
questions.answer: The Soviet economy faced serious problems and could not keep up with the arms race. Reforms by Gorbachev and demands for change in Eastern Europe weakened the Soviet bloc.
keyPoints: Reforms and weakening of the Soviet bloc
questions.explanation: Several internal and external factors ended the rivalry.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: A city with a population of one million or more is often called
questions.explanation: Cities of a million or more people are called million-plus cities.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: Which authority conducts the Census of India?
options: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner
questions.explanation: The census is conducted under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: Why do many agricultural societies traditionally have high birth rates?
options: Children are seen as helpers on the farm
Birth rates are zero in villages
questions.explanation: Children contribute labour in farming households.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: A sex ratio of 900 means
questions.explanation: 900 females per 1000 males shows fewer females than males.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: Why are hilly and mountainous regions often thinly populated?
options: Steep slopes, thin soil and poor access limit farming and settlement
They have no rivers at all
questions.explanation: Terrain restricts agriculture and communication.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: Why do big metropolitan cities have a very high population density?
options: They concentrate jobs and services in a limited space
They have very large areas per person
questions.explanation: Jobs and services draw people into limited urban space.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: State two effects of rapid population growth on resources.
questions.answer: Rapid growth increases demand for food, water, housing and energy, which can strain supplies. It can also lead to overuse of land and forests, causing environmental damage.
keyPoints: Greater demand for food, water and housing
questions.explanation: More people place greater demand on limited resources.

questions.topic: Geography: population and human settlements
questions.q: How can a high dependency ratio affect a country's economy?
questions.answer: A high dependency ratio means many children or elderly depend on fewer working-age people. This can reduce savings, and raise spending needed on education, health and care.
keyPoints: Higher spending on education, health and care
questions.explanation: A larger dependent population places a burden on workers and government.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Bauxite is the main ore of which metal?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Which of these is a cash crop?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is grown mainly for sale.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Nuclear power plants use which element as fuel?
questions.explanation: Uranium is the main nuclear fuel.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: The Bhakra Nangal project is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra dam stands on the Sutlej.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: How does terrace farming help in hilly areas?
options: It reduces soil erosion and allows cultivation on slopes
questions.explanation: Terraces slow run-off and hold soil.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Why is crop diversification encouraged?
options: It ensures every crop fails together
It lowers risk from failure of a single crop and can help maintain soil health
questions.explanation: Growing several crops spreads risk.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Why is soil erosion a serious problem? State two methods of controlling it.
questions.answer: Erosion removes fertile topsoil, lowering yields and degrading land. It can be reduced by planting trees and grass cover, terracing and contour ploughing.
questions.explanation: Soil is a slowly renewed resource that needs protection.

questions.topic: Geography: resources, agriculture and industry
questions.q: Explain briefly Weber's least cost theory of industrial location.
questions.answer: Alfred Weber argued that an industry locates where its total costs are lowest. He gave most weight to transport cost, and also considered labour cost and the advantage of clustering.
questions.explanation: Weber's theory explains location by cost minimisation.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Trade between two countries is called
questions.explanation: Bilateral trade takes place between two countries.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Exports of goods minus imports of goods is called
questions.explanation: That is the balance of trade.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Which of these is an advantage of railways?
options: Suited to carrying heavy goods and many passengers over long distances
questions.explanation: Railways are efficient for bulk and long-distance transport.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Which of these ports is on India's east coast?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam lies on the Bay of Bengal coast.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Why do countries impose tariffs on imports?
options: To protect domestic industries and raise revenue
To lower all prices to zero
questions.explanation: Tariffs raise the price of imports and bring in revenue.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Why is the Suez Canal important to trade between India and Europe?
options: It connects India with Africa by rail
It shortens the sea route compared with going around Africa
questions.explanation: Ships avoid the long voyage around the Cape of Good Hope.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: What is meant by human development?
questions.answer: Human development means widening people's choices and improving their lives, mainly through better health, education and access to resources. It looks at what people can do and be, not only at income.
questions.explanation: The idea was popularised by Mahbub ul Haq and the UNDP.

questions.topic: Geography: transport, trade and human development
questions.q: Why do countries trade with one another?
questions.answer: Resources and skills are unevenly spread, so countries import what they lack and export what they produce well. Specialisation based on comparative advantage and demand for variety also encourage trade.
questions.explanation: Trade lets countries benefit from differences in resources and skills.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: Which of these is a function of money?
options: Acting as a medium of exchange
questions.explanation: Money makes exchange easy.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.explanation: The RBI was established in 1935.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP is
questions.explanation: Real GDP removes the effect of price changes.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: The Consumer Price Index measures
options: the change in retail prices of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by consumers
questions.explanation: CPI tracks price changes for a basket of consumer goods and services.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: Why does a central bank conduct open market operations?
options: To adjust the money supply by buying or selling government securities
questions.explanation: Buying securities adds money to the system and selling securities withdraws it.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: Why can a rise in investment raise national income by more than the initial amount?
options: Because of the multiplier effect, as spending is re-spent and creates more income
questions.explanation: Each round of spending becomes income for others, who spend again.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: State two reasons why people hold money.
questions.answer: People hold money for transactions, to buy goods and services in daily life. They also keep it as a precaution for emergencies, and some hold it for speculative reasons.
questions.explanation: These are the standard motives for demanding money.

questions.topic: Economics: national income, money and banking
questions.q: Distinguish between GDP and GNP.
questions.answer: GDP counts the value of final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory. GNP adds net factor income from abroad, so it counts the output of a country's residents wherever they work.
keyPoints: GNP adds net factor income from abroad
questions.explanation: The difference is whether income earned abroad is included.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: The government's yearly statement of expected receipts and expenditure is called the
questions.explanation: That statement is the budget.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: Which of these is a non-tax receipt of the government?
questions.explanation: Interest and dividends are non-tax revenue.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: In a flexible exchange rate system, the rate is determined by
options: the demand and supply of foreign exchange in the market
a fixed decision of the government
questions.explanation: The market forces of demand and supply set the rate.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: Which was an aim of liberalisation after 1991?
options: Reducing government control over private enterprise and opening the economy to foreign trade
Raising import duties to the maximum
questions.explanation: Liberalisation reduced controls and encouraged competition.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: Why was the Green Revolution important for India's development?
options: Higher-yielding varieties raised foodgrain output and reduced dependence on imports
questions.explanation: Output rose, improving food security.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: Why is spending on education and health called investment in human capital?
options: It improves the skills and productivity of workers
It reduces the number of workers
It has no effect on output
questions.explanation: Better skills and health raise productivity.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: What is the informal sector? State two features.
questions.answer: The informal sector consists of enterprises and workers not covered by formal regulation or registration. Its features include low and irregular earnings and little job security or social protection.
questions.explanation: A large share of workers in India are in the informal sector.

questions.topic: Economics: budget, external sector and development since 1991
questions.q: Describe one benefit and one problem that have been linked with economic reforms since 1991.
questions.answer: A benefit is higher growth and greater choice for consumers because of competition and openness. A problem is that gains were uneven, and some small producers found it hard to compete.
keyPoints: Problem: uneven gains or pressure on small producers
questions.explanation: Reforms had both gains and costs.
